title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
content_md: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. The extension used the version number 2.1.313 and was distributed between 2:27 a.m. and 1:35 p.m. Pacific Time. Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built from Microsoft’s open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), with support for VS Code extensions. Anthropic’s Claude Code extension brings its AI coding assistant directly into compatible editors, helping developers write and debug code using natural-language instructions. Cursor says Anthropic did not develop the malicious extension but has not explained how attackers distributed the compromised package under Anthropic's name. "Between about 2:27 am PT and 1:35 pm PT today, a maliciously modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was made available in the Cursor VS Code extension Marketplace," warned Cursor . "The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor." Researchers at Phorion and OpenSourceMalware found that the attackers inserted a malicious JavaScript loader at the beginning of the extension's extension.js file, leaving the legitimate extension code otherwise unchanged.
